note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: What do existing records show about this compressor's recycle or blow-off duty?

evidence.text: equipment K-R reads "K-R Fictional rotary screw air compressor K-R"
final element RV-R reads "RV-R Recycle/bypass candidate; fictional unverified model association" at K-R
K-R machine_class = "rotary screw"; present; meaning and suitability unverified
K-R service = "air"; present; meaning and suitability unverified

data_requests.item: Existing control records, machine/service and operating-mode basis
where: site records: retained operating/control records with exact machine and valve IDs, record revision and locator
historian or DCS trend for RV-R (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: existing approved control documentation, if applicable; controller demand/output is not measured travel or flow
data_requests.how: Start with existing records and check machine class, service and duty. Keep exact machine, valve and record IDs, revision, locator and supplied limitations. Resolve foreign, unknown or shared targets with the record owner; a model association does not verify installed pairing or sibling coverage. Distinguish controller demand/output, actual valve travel and measured flow, including units, quality and reference conditions. Select a representative period from demand and relevant normal, turndown, startup/shutdown and upset coverage, not a fixed month. Acknowledge suitable existing evidence and request only the remaining gaps.

data_requests.item: Applicable machine-protection basis and qualified review
where: site records: current site protection/control basis, applicable revision, conditions and responsible reviewer
the vendor datasheet: the appropriate machine-specific operating envelope and protection guidance for the declared service
data_requests.how: Review existing manufacturer/site records with the responsible machinery and controls engineers. Establish applicability to this machine, service, conditions and revision before interpreting a surge line or controller margin. A generic, obsolete or other-machine map cannot establish an excessive margin. Retain unresolved applicability and missing review; do not change settings, operate a valve or induce surge to answer this screen.

data_requests.item: Time-aligned real-power, pressure and flow evidence
where: site records: existing energy/operating records with measurement basis, units, quality, time and individual/shared machine coverage
data_requests.how: Check existing records for time-aligned real input power, pressure, flow and operating conditions over the selected duty. Separate measured real power from estimates, nameplate ratings and apparent quantities. Check each record against the exact machine(s) and time covered. Reuse a shared record when its reviewed scope covers the named machines and time; do not infer missing individual coverage from a sibling trace. Keep zero, null and unknown values and limitations explicit. Agree any remaining evidence plan with the responsible owner; no new export, walkdown or test is compulsory when suitable records already exist.

questions.decision_rule: Review the evidence and remaining gaps with the responsible process, controls and machinery engineers. Recycle/blow-off activity can reflect protection and demand; an open valve or a generic margin alone does not establish waste. Turndown/upset-only opening alone neither closes the investigation nor proves a deficiency. Acknowledge suitable working evidence and record the basis for concluding or continuing this screening investigation, its next owner and unresolved questions. No retrofit or quantified saving follows from this screen.

typical_benefit.wording: Blow-off "is a waste of energy and should be used only where necessary to avoid surge." Inlet throttling: "Capacity can typically be reduced from 100 percent capacity to about 70-80 percent with reasonable energy reduction." No % saving stated.
source_titles: S11: Improving Compressed Air System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 3rd ed. (DOE + Compressed Air Challenge)

questions.limits: S11 describes compressed-air systems, including centrifugal-air controls; its examples and figures do not automatically apply to process gas, rotary or unknown machines. Establish machine/service applicability first. Supplied machine_class, service and control_records values are unverified claims, including approval/quality fields; showing them does not authenticate their source or establish installed function, protection adequacy or complete coverage. Keep unmatched records, unclear shared coverage and missing reference conditions unresolved. This screen authorizes no operation, test or protection/settings change; any proposed change needs responsible machinery/vendor expertise and the company change-review process.

questions.question: Does the air compressor lack enough storage for intermittent large users?

evidence.text: equipment K-R reads "K-R Fictional rotary screw air compressor K-R"
no receiver or air storage anywhere in the model

where: a walkdown: data-log compressor load and header pressure for a week

questions.decision_rule: Add storage when short peaks force an extra compressor on.

typical_benefit.wording: Storage "may allow such a compressor to be turned off." No % stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.422x (category only) (IAC/ITAC browse page: 8,589 recommendations, 1.2 yr average payback, 46.5% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S10: Compressed Air Tip #9, Compressed Air Storage Strategies (DOE/GO-102004-1965)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: Is air compressor heat rejected when it could heat something?

evidence.text: equipment K-R reads "K-R Fictional rotary screw air compressor K-R"

data_requests.item: Load hours and a nearby heat sink
where: a walkdown: space or water heating needs nearby

questions.decision_rule: Worth a look when the compressor runs long hours and a low-temperature heat user is nearby.

typical_benefit.wording: "As much as 80 to 93 percent of the electrical energy" becomes heat; recovery "anywhere from 50 to 90 percent of this".
source_titles: S11: Improving Compressed Air System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 3rd ed. (DOE + Compressed Air Challenge)

questions.question: What source-labelled trip or interlock records apply to each rotating or fired machine, and what remains unverified?

evidence.text: equipment K-R reads "K-R Fictional rotary screw air compressor K-R"
equipment K-U reads "K-U Fictional compressor K-U"

where: site records: cause-and-effect matrix, HAZOP and LOPA reports
data_requests.how: Review existing cause-and-effect, governing requirements and configuration records for each named machine, with their revisions and applicability. Retain supplied trip/switch indications as candidates; a drawing label or an unrelated function does not settle the records or establish effective, tested protection. Missing model information is not evidence that installed protection is absent.

where: site records: source-labelled function identifiers, initiating measurements, final elements and protected-machine targets, shared scope and revisions; governing requirements and validation/test evidence where applicable
DCS/PLC configuration: existing configuration and its documented measurement/action/final-element identities, read through the approved site process
data_requests.how: Keep each machine in the review even where a switch or trip is supplied. Retain all explicit shared targets and supplied qualifiers; unknown or contradictory targets remain unresolved. Same-model text or nearby equipment does not prove function coverage. Record a responsible person or authority separately from protected-machine association; neither is inferred here. This requests record review, not a new test, safety design or operating action.

questions.decision_rule: A qualified site review may resolve the source-labelled machine/function associations and remaining record requests using applicable current evidence. A supplied trip, switch, cause/effect row or shared-function label alone establishes neither complete coverage nor installed protection adequacy. This screen grants no acceptance or authority and performs no safety validation.

typical_benefit.wording: Safety benefit; no energy source. Present it as a question to verify, not a finding.

questions.limits: P&IDs often leave trips to separate cause-and-effect records. Missing or unknown model evidence does not establish missing installed protection. Supplied associations, shared targets, revisions and contradictions require review; no machine, person owner, approval, tested condition or effective protection is inferred. C9 has no primary safety-design source cited in the catalog and remains a question for record review, not safety design, SIL assignment, a legal-compliance assessment or an operating recommendation.
